# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 19 (SOPHIA Consensus)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 19
**Agent:** SOPHIA (Consensus)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Consensus Translation

1. But the way of the Black One is crooked and full of cursing; for it is a way of eternal death with punishment, in which are the things that destroy souls: idolatry, arrogance, pride of power, hypocrisy, duplicity, adultery, murder, robbery, conceit, transgression, deceit, malice, self-will, sorcery, magic, covetousness, absence of the fear of God.
2. It is the way of persecutors of the good, haters of truth, lovers of falsehood — who do not know the reward of righteousness, who do not cleave to the good nor to righteous judgment, who do not attend to the widow and the orphan, who watch not for the fear of God but for what is evil — from whom meekness and patience are far removed, who love vanity and pursue reward, who have no compassion on the poor, who do not toil for the oppressed, who are ready to slander, who do not acknowledge their Maker, who are murderers of children and corrupters of what God has molded, who turn away from the needy, who oppress the afflicted, who are advocates of the rich, lawless judges of the poor, utterly sinful in every respect.

---

## Council Notes

- vv.1-2: The Way of Darkness / Way of the Black One corresponds to Didache 5, which has a shorter parallel list. Barnabas's list is longer and more rhetorically developed.
- v.1: The list of vices in v.1 (16 items) follows a standard Hellenistic vice-list form; cf. Romans 1:29-31; Galatians 5:19-21; 1 Corinthians 6:9-10. The combination of Jewish ethical tradition and Hellenistic form is characteristic of Alexandrian Jewish-Christian synthesis.
- v.2: "Murderers of children and corrupters of what God has molded" — the Two Ways' prohibition of abortion/infanticide (from ch. 18) reappears on the negative side as a defining characteristic of the Way of Darkness. The phrase "corrupters of what God has molded" (*phthoreis plasmatos theou*) implies that human life as God's handiwork (*plasma*) is sacred.
- v.2: "Advocates of the rich, lawless judges of the poor" — the social-justice critique is prominent in the Way of Darkness; the corruption of the justice system on behalf of the wealthy is one of the gravest sins catalogued. Cf. Amos 2:6-7; Isaiah 10:1-2.
